entry.summary:

Source: @javadimr

If opposition to Rasaei's prison sentence is not grounded in a general defense of freedom of expression, the right to criticize those in power, and the necessity of tolerance, and rests only on "why didn't you arrest others?" or "he's worked hard," then what we're dealing with is a demand for "judicial immunity for the hard core": a kind of political tribalism and double standard that downgrades a universal right to a group privilege.

entry.title: [javadimr] "Either we build security together, or [we will be forced to] endure insecurity…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @javadimr

"Either we build security together, or [we will be forced to] endure insecurity together." Pezeshkian's words at the United Nations sum up the logic of interdependence: security—whether national or regional—and stability are collective goods; if they are not for everyone, they will not remain sustainable for anyone. A policy of exclusion makes the cost of insecurity everyone's burden.

entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @javadimr

Blocking a national ID and the mobile number linked to it, in a networked society, is not merely a technical restriction; it is a form of "punitive digital exclusion" and an informal confinement from social life and civic engagement. Driving protesters to despair will neither bring them to heel nor scare others straight; it only widens the unbridgeable gaps.
